title: Pareto Kernel Tier Planner: multi-objective kernel selection with warm-replay autotune
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Problem: Our runtime must pick the concrete kernel implementation for attention and other primitives across heterogeneous GPU families and varying request token lengths. Current heuristics optimize a single metric (latency mean) and either miss cost savings at larger batch sizes or fail to control tail latency. This ticket proposes a Pareto-driven kernel tier planner (PKTP) that builds a compact frontier of trade-offs (latency p50/p95, cost-per-token, throughput) per (model variant, hw-class, token-length bucket, batch size) and picks an operating point based on policy and SLOs. PKTP uses a warm-replay of historical traces to jump-start profiles, continuously refines candidates online with budgeted exploration, and supports emergency fallback to safe kernels when SLOs degrade.
acceptance_criteria:
1) PKTP produces a per-route kernel recommendation file and a justification metric-set for at least three model variants (small/medium/large) across two GPU classes (A100, H100) and at least four token-length buckets.
2) In staging, overall token cost decreases by >=6% for a mixed workload compared to baseline heuristics while maintaining p95 latency within configured SLOs for 99% of requests.
3) Telemetry surfaces decisions per-request and exposes confidence score, exploration flag, and warm-replay provenance.
4) Rollout can be toggled per-route and automatically falls back to the prefill-safe kernel when p95 exceeds SLO for >1 minute.
5) Code merged with tests and an end-to-end Canary in runtime-1.20 release branch.
experiment_plan: Phase A: Offline profiling - run microbench harness across kernels and cache results grouped by (arch, model, tokens, batch). Phase B: Warm-replay seeding - ingest 30 days of production traces into the profiler and build initial candidate frontier. Phase C: Staging - enable PKTP for 10% traffic with exploration budget 5% of requests; collect cost/latency/throughput. Phase D: Canary - 1 region, rollback guard, SLO alarms enabled. Phase E: Gradual ramp to 100% with continuous monitoring.
metrics: Primary: cost_per_token (USD equivalent), latency_p50, latency_p95. Secondary: throughput_tps, kernel_switch_rate, exploration_request_fraction, SLO_violation_count. Observability: histogram-backed latency by kernel_id and token_bucket, time-series of frontier size.
rollout_plan: Staging (internal only) -> Canary (1 region) -> Region ramp (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) if SLOs hold. Each stage gated by automated checks: p95 <= SLO + 5ms, cost_per_token regression < 1% worse than baseline, kernel_switch_rate < configured threshold. Emergency rollback triggers: sustained SLO violation for >1 minute or error-rate spike >2x baseline.
risks_mitigation: Risk: exploration can introduce high-latency kernels. Mitigation: hard cap on exploration fraction and an immediate per-request fallback if decode time exceeds safety threshold. Risk: noisy warm-replay seeding leading to poor frontier. Mitigation: apply recency-weighted smoothing and drop outliers beyond 99.9th percentile. Risk: excessive kernel churn increases instability. Mitigation: hysteresis in policy and minimum dwell time per kernel before reconsideration.
